title: A complete characterization of eventually entanglement breaking unital quantum channels
authors: B. V. Rajarama Bhat, Pankaj Dey, Biswarup Saha
abstract: We obtain a complete characterization of eventually entanglement breaking (EEB) unital channels in terms of some simple commutation properties of their eigenvectors. Specifically, the following properties are equivalent for a unital channel: (i) it is EEB; (ii) it is eventually positive partial transpose (PPT); (iii) it is eventually mixed twisted dephasing; and (iv) its eigenvectors corresponding to non-zero eigenvalues commute with all its peripheral eigenvectors. Similar results hold for one-parameter semigroups of unital quantum channels, where continuity forces such semigroups to become primitive. We employ a matrix integral technique inspired by a result of Watrous. We also characterize the extreme points of the convex set of unital EB channels and, using this characterization and the theory of equiangular tight frames (ETFs), identify several extreme points beyond the twisted dephasing channels.
summary: This theoretical paper fully characterizes eventually entanglement breaking (EEB) unital quantum channels by proving the equivalence of several complex properties, such as being eventually PPT or eventually mixed twisted dephasing. Using advanced tools like matrix integrals, it extends these findings to continuous time quantum Markov semigroups, showing that these dynamics are equivalent to the semigroup being primitive and converging to the maximally mixed state.
main_problem: The paper aims to provide a complete mathematical characterization of eventually entanglement breaking (EEB) unital quantum channels.
main_result: It establishes the equivalence of several properties for unital channels, including being EEB, eventually PPT, eventually mixed twisted dephasing, and a specific commutation relation among eigenvectors.
method: The authors employ advanced mathematical techniques, including matrix integrals inspired by Watrous, and utilize the theory of equiangular tight frames (ETFs) to characterize extreme points.
model_or_system: The study focuses on quantum channels, which are completely positive and trace-preserving linear maps acting on matrix algebras ($M_d$). The analysis extends to continuous time via quantum Markov semigroups.
key_observables: The commutation property of eigenvectors corresponding to non-zero eigenvalues with peripheral eigenvectors, and the structure of the Choi matrix $J(\varphi)$.
important_parameters: The dimension $d$ of the system, and the time parameter $t$ for continuous semigroups.
main_assumptions: The analysis heavily relies on the assumption that the quantum channel under consideration is unital.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the equivalence relationships between various channel properties (EB, MTD, PPT, etc.) in discrete time, while Figure 2 shows the analogous equivalences for continuous time semigroups.
paper_structure: The paper first characterizes EB maps using the Choi-Jamiołkowski isomorphism, then extends this to the 'eventually' regime (EEB), establishing equivalences between EEB, eventual PPT, and eventual MTD. It then applies these concepts to continuous time semigroups, proving that these properties are equivalent to the semigroup being primitive and converging to the maximally mixed state.
why_interesting: This work provides deep structural insights into the long-term dynamics of open quantum systems, linking concepts like entanglement breaking, quantum process tomography (PPT), and spectral properties (primitivity) into a single, unified mathematical framework.
